evidence.claim: The Ministry of Rural Development said that in FY2021-22 MGNREGS had completed 83.82 lakh works and had 133.09 lakh works ongoing, while remaining a demand-driven wage-employment program.
evidence.title: Study to Assess the Impact of MGNREGS
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The Ministry of Rural Development said that in FY2021-22 MGNREGS had completed 83.82 lakh works and had 133.09 lakh works ongoing, while remaining a demand-driven wage-employment program.
evidence.source_locator: opening lines and FY2021-22 performance summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry release with concrete implementation statistics.
evidence.period_fit: Covers the fiscal year ending in 2022 and thus the target year period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Modi-led central government, though state execution is crucial for delivery.
contrary_evidence: The release is descriptive of works and does not show how well wages or job quality translated into long-term gains.

evidence.claim: As of 30 November 2022, 1,31,150 Health and Wellness Centres were functional, and PM-JAY had 7.87 crore registered beneficiary households, about 73% of the targeted households.
evidence.title: Audit Report No. 11 of 2023: Performance Audit of Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
evidence.publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
evidence.excerpt: As of 30 November 2022, 1,31,150 Health and Wellness Centres were functional, and PM-JAY had 7.87 crore registered beneficiary households, about 73% of the targeted households.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent statutory audit with concrete counts and a direct 2022 status snapshot.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective evidence about the 2022 target period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for central scheme design and oversight; actual service use still depends on state, hospital, and household access.
contrary_evidence: Registration and functional-centre counts do not by themselves prove adequate care quality or full coverage of the poorest.

evidence.claim: NITI Aayog said Parameswaran Iyer became its CEO on 11 July 2022 and highlighted over 25 years of water-and-sanitation experience, including spearheading the Swachh Bharat Mission and serving as Secretary in the Drinking Water and Sanitation ministry.
evidence.title: NITI Aayog Welcomes Parameswaran Iyer as Its CEO
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: NITI Aayog said Parameswaran Iyer became its CEO on 11 July 2022 and highlighted over 25 years of water-and-sanitation experience, including spearheading the Swachh Bharat Mission and serving as Secretary in the Drinking Water and Sanitation ministry.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary appointment release with a detailed professional background and exact date.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong: PMO-linked senior administrative appointment; positive for professional staffing, though not proof that every appointment was merit-only.
contrary_evidence: The appointment does not alone demonstrate broader anti-nepotism practice across government.

evidence.claim: The NITI Aayog circulars page publicly lists the July 2022 appointment notification for Shri Parameswaran Iyer as CEO and the December 2022 appointment notification for Shri Arvind Virmani as Member.
evidence.title: NITI Aayog (notifications index)
evidence.publication_date: 2022-12-01 (best available for the listed notification entry)
evidence.excerpt: The NITI Aayog circulars page publicly lists the July 2022 appointment notification for Shri Parameswaran Iyer as CEO and the December 2022 appointment notification for Shri Arvind Virmani as Member.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official public index of notifications, directly linking the relevant 2022 appointment entries.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong at the level of transparency around appointments; limited because the index does not explain appointment criteria or independence.
contrary_evidence: A public notification list is not evidence that all appointments were merit-based.

evidence.claim: PRS summarized the budget as raising capital expenditure by 24.5 percent to Rs 7,50,246 crore and increasing allocations for roads, Jal Jeevan Mission, National Education Mission, women and child welfare, SC/ST, and the North Eastern Region.
evidence.title: Union Budget 2022-23 Analysis
evidence.excerpt: PRS summarized the budget as raising capital expenditure by 24.5 percent to Rs 7,50,246 crore and increasing allocations for roads, Jal Jeevan Mission, National Education Mission, women and child welfare, SC/ST, and the North Eastern Region.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent legislative research that directly parses the union budget documents and reproduces the main numerical choices.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about the 2022-23 budget adopted during the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for central budget priorities; weaker for downstream implementation because this is a plan document.
contrary_evidence: Budgeted allocations are not the same as delivered outcomes.
Some spending lines did not automatically convert into measurable 2022 gains.

evidence.claim: Modi said PM GatiShakti would change infrastructure planning, implementation, and monitoring; he said more than 400 data layers were available and 24 digital systems from 6 ministries were being integrated through ULIP to reduce logistics costs.
evidence.title: PM addresses post-budget webinar on vision of 'GatiShakti'
evidence.excerpt: Modi said PM GatiShakti would change infrastructure planning, implementation, and monitoring; he said more than 400 data layers were available and 24 digital systems from 6 ministries were being integrated through ULIP to reduce logistics costs.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official transcript of the PM's own explanation of the program, strong for strategy and intended mechanism but not independent proof of final performance.
evidence.period_fit: Within the target year and explicitly tied to Union Budget 2022 and 2022 implementation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High for strategic direction and coordination model; lower for actual delivery because this is still a declared implementation framework.
contrary_evidence: The webinar is aspirational and does not itself show completion.
Claims about efficiency still need independent outcome checks.

evidence.claim: The audit says 131,150 Health and Wellness Centres were functional as of 30 November 2022, the government approved expansion of PMJAY to 12 crore families in January 2022, and 7.87 crore beneficiary households were registered, about 73 percent of the target.
evidence.title: Report No. 11 of 2023 - Performance Audit of Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
evidence.publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
evidence.excerpt: The audit says 131,150 Health and Wellness Centres were functional as of 30 November 2022, the government approved expansion of PMJAY to 12 crore families in January 2022, and 7.87 crore beneficiary households were registered, about 73 percent of the target.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent constitutional audit with concrete operational numbers covering the target period through late 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Audit published in 2023 but explicitly covers implementation through 30 November 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for central scheme design and funding; implementation also depends on the National Health Authority and state health systems.
contrary_evidence: Registration fell short of the target household base.
The audit shows reach, but not full completion.

evidence.claim: The IMF said the authorities responded to post-pandemic shocks with fiscal policy support to vulnerable groups and front-loaded monetary tightening; it also said digital public infrastructure enabled rapid support deployment and financial inclusion, and that real GDP grew 8.7 percent in FY2021/22.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation with India
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said the authorities responded to post-pandemic shocks with fiscal policy support to vulnerable groups and front-loaded monetary tightening; it also said digital public infrastructure enabled rapid support deployment and financial inclusion, and that real GDP grew 8.7 percent in FY2021/22.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral surveillance with specific quantitative claims, though some policy levers were RBI-led and some outcomes reflect inherited recovery dynamics.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about 2022 policy response and FY2021/22 outcomes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for fiscal support and digital public infrastructure; mixed for monetary tightening because the RBI is institutionally independent.
contrary_evidence: Inflation remained elevated and growth was expected to moderate.
Some key levers were shared with or delegated to the RBI rather than controlled solely by Modi.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said India was relatively well positioned to weather global spillovers, that policy reforms and prudent regulatory measures improved resilience, and that market borrowings improved the transparency and credibility of fiscal policy.
evidence.title: India Better Positioned to Navigate Global Headwinds Than Other Major Emerging Economies: New World Bank Report
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said India was relatively well positioned to weather global spillovers, that policy reforms and prudent regulatory measures improved resilience, and that market borrowings improved the transparency and credibility of fiscal policy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral assessment with clear links between reforms and macro resilience, though some reforms predate 2022 and some outcomes are indirect.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and evaluating 2022 conditions and policy response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate, because the report combines Modi-era reforms, RBI actions, and inherited macro buffers.
contrary_evidence: External shocks and a widening current-account deficit still weighed on growth.
The report is favorable but not a clean ruler-only causal finding.

evidence.claim: By 16 November 2022, PM GatiShakti had incorporated more than 1,900 GIS data layers, and officials said over 250 infrastructure projects had been examined using the platform in the previous year, with stalled projects being expedited.
evidence.title: Shri Piyush Goyal reviews progress of PM GatiShakti National Master Plan
evidence.excerpt: By 16 November 2022, PM GatiShakti had incorporated more than 1,900 GIS data layers, and officials said over 250 infrastructure projects had been examined using the platform in the previous year, with stalled projects being expedited.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Concrete official progress report with specific counts and a contemporaneous description of implementation, though it remains a government self-report.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and about 2022 implementation progress.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate to strong for Modi's governing program; the mechanism is cabinet-led and shared across ministries and states.
contrary_evidence: Self-reported progress is not independent proof of cost reduction or completion quality.
The report does not isolate Modi personally from the broader government machine.

evidence.claim: The IMF reported that India's digital payment volume had grown about 50 percent annually over five years, UPI transactions more than doubled to 5.86 billion in June 2022, and a feature-phone UPI rollout could connect about 400 million users in rural areas.
evidence.title: How India's Central Bank Helped Spur a Digital Payments Boom
evidence.excerpt: The IMF reported that India's digital payment volume had grown about 50 percent annually over five years, UPI transactions more than doubled to 5.86 billion in June 2022, and a feature-phone UPI rollout could connect about 400 million users in rural areas.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent IMF feature with concrete figures and a clear description of the operating mechanism.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and about an active 2022 outcome.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but meaningful. The article supports the Modi-era digital-public-infrastructure program, but the implementation engine also includes RBI and NPCI.
contrary_evidence: The article credits the RBI and ecosystem partners heavily, so attribution to Modi is shared rather than exclusive.
Digital-payment growth is not the same as broad labor-market or income gains.

Independent corroboration that 2022 restraint rhetoric changed actual readiness or crisis procedures
Cleaner evidence on whether the 2022 proliferation/export-control steps were implemented effectively rather than merely announced
Direct evidence that Modi personally drove a consequential ceasefire or settlement outcome rather than issuing restraint rhetoric
Clearer internal rationale for India's abstentions on the Ukraine votes
Direct evidence of Modi's personal intervention or deliberate omission after notice in specific 2022 abuse episodes
Better evidence on prosecution, discipline, or remedy after 2022 custodial, demolition, and communal-violence episodes
Direct evidence that Modi strengthened independent courts, legislatures, audit bodies, or oversight institutions when they constrained him
Cleaner central-attribution evidence for internet shutdowns and content-removal orders
Household-level distributional evidence showing how 2022 gains reached poorer households, regions, and groups
Cleaner evidence on business favoritism, procurement, and connected conglomerate advantages in 2022
Independent outcome evaluations of service quality, leakage, and distribution for PM POSHAN, PM-JAY, PM-KISAN, and JJM
Better district-, caste-, tribe-, and gender-disaggregated evidence on who gained and who remained excluded
Direct 2022 evidence of deliberate falsehood, correction, or concealment by Modi on a matter tied to power or reputation
Independent evidence on PM CARES transparency, procurement, or benefit from office that links personally to Modi rather than just the PMO
Stronger evidence on whether senior appointments were made for competence, loyalty, or patronage in 2022
Independent evaluation of whether PM GatiShakti actually reduced logistics costs, sped projects, or improved coordination
Cleaner attribution between Modi, the Finance Ministry, the RBI, states, and private actors on the macro and digital outcomes
